name: Do I need a building permit to replace a shower in Denver or Centennial?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a building permit to replace a shower in Denver or Centennial?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, including Centennial and Parker, a permit is typically required if the shower installation involves relocating plumbing lines, moving electrical switches, or modifying structural walls. Simple surface-level replacements of fixtures or tile in an identical footprint may not require a permit depending on local municipal rules. When building out custom walk-in showers that alter drain sizing or rough plumbing, pulling a permit ensures the work meets regional plumbing codes and passes required rough-in and final inspections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are usually required when moving plumbing pipes, altering drainage, or changing wall framing, but like-for-like fixture swaps often do not need one.
